newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British flags fly at half mast in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: British flags fly at half mast in Hong Kong.

text.p: The Hong Kong colonial government ordered all British flags to fly at half-mast on Thursday in a gesture of respect to the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

"Flags on all government buildings will be flown at half-mast for one day (from) noon (0400 GMT) today as a mark of respect for Deng Xiaoping, who passed away on Wednesday," a Hong Kong government statement said.

Deng, whose 18 years of reform transformed China from an impoverished Stalinist state to emerging economic superpower, died of respiratory failure in an advanced stage of Parkinson's disease. He was 92.
Chinese flags in the territory also flew at half mast.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, will return to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, a date now 131 days away.
